originalWholeQuestion.question: Which principle best characterizes clinical and imaging diagnosis?
choices: A new infiltrate plus infectious clinical evidence supports HAP or VAP, but no gold standard exists
Two antipseudomonal agents from different classes are reserved for defined resistance risk, poor local susceptibility, or unknown data
The 2026 consensus reserves true beta-lactam dose individualization for regimens informed by measured patient concentrations
In eligible mechanically ventilated adults, use early enteral rather than parenteral nutrition; change ventilator circuits when visibly soiled or malfunctioning, or as the manufacturer instructs
originalWholeQuestion.rationale: Critical illness creates many noninfectious mimics

choiceEvaluations.choice: A new infiltrate plus infectious clinical evidence supports HAP or VAP, but no gold standard exists
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Correct: Definitions combines a new infiltrate with clinical evidence of infectious origin and explicitly states no diagnostic gold standard.

choiceEvaluations.choice: A new infiltrate alone proves that the lung abnormality has an infectious cause
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: imaging alone omits the required clinical evidence of infectious origin.

choiceEvaluations.choice: Purulent secretions alone provide a definitive diagnosis regardless of imaging or clinical trajectory
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: purulent secretions are one clinical feature, not a stand-alone definitive diagnostic test.

choiceEvaluations.choice: Clinical evidence can be ignored once an imaging abnormality is present
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: the definition requires integration of clinical evidence with imaging.

originalWholeQuestion.question: Which principle best characterizes HAP MSSA and gram-negative frame?
choices: Empiric HAP therapy generally covers MSSA and Pseudomonas-active gram-negative organisms
The 2026 consensus reserves true beta-lactam dose individualization for regimens informed by measured patient concentrations
In eligible mechanically ventilated adults, use early enteral rather than parenteral nutrition; change ventilator circuits when visibly soiled or malfunctioning, or as the manufacturer instructs
Colonization of an endotracheal tube does not prove invasive pneumonia
originalWholeQuestion.rationale: Nosocomial gram-negative coverage is part of the baseline frame

sourceSections: ATS/IDSA 2016 XII recommendations1,1.i-iii,2; Table4; native PDF pages5-6

choiceEvaluations.choice: Empiric HAP therapy covers S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, and other gram-negative bacilli, with MRSA coverage when indicated
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Correct: XII recommends S. aureus and P. aeruginosa/other gram-negative coverage; MRSA coverage is risk-guided.

choiceEvaluations.choice: Empiric HAP therapy can cover gram-negative bacilli alone and omit all S. aureus coverage
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: omission of all S. aureus activity contradicts XII.1.

choiceEvaluations.choice: Empiric HAP therapy can cover MSSA alone and omit P. aeruginosa and other gram-negative bacilli
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: MSSA-only activity omits the gram-negative coverage recommended by XII.2.

choiceEvaluations.choice: Empiric HAP therapy needs P. aeruginosa coverage only after a positive culture has already identified it
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: XII.2 applies to patients being treated empirically, before a positive organism-identifying culture is required.

originalWholeQuestion.question: Which principle best characterizes definitive MRSA therapy?
choices: Vancomycin or linezolid is recommended for proven MRSA HAP or VAP
In eligible mechanically ventilated adults, use early enteral rather than parenteral nutrition; change ventilator circuits when visibly soiled or malfunctioning, or as the manufacturer instructs
Colonization of an endotracheal tube does not prove invasive pneumonia
Use two antipseudomonal classes when resistance risk exists, more than 10 percent of isolates resist the proposed monotherapy, or susceptibility data are unavailable

sourceSections: ATS/IDSA 2016 XV recommendation1 and remarks; native PDF page6
RxPrep2023 daptomycin and oxazolidinones, printed358/PDF366; native table inspected

choiceEvaluations.choice: Vancomycin or linezolid is recommended for proven MRSA HAP or VAP
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Correct: XV recommends either vancomycin or linezolid for MRSA HAP/VAP.

choiceEvaluations.choice: Choose daptomycin for MRSA HAP or VAP because its bloodstream activity guarantees lung activity
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: the book expressly excludes daptomycin for pneumonia because surfactant inactivates it.

choiceEvaluations.choice: Treat proven MRSA HAP or VAP with an MSSA-only antibiotic instead of MRSA-active therapy
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: an MSSA-only antibiotic cannot replace the MRSA-active therapy recommended for proven MRSA pneumonia.

choiceEvaluations.choice: Use an antipseudomonal agent with no MRSA activity as the sole definitive treatment for proven MRSA HAP or VAP
choiceEvaluations.evaluation: Incorrect: a drug lacking MRSA activity cannot serve as sole definitive treatment for proven MRSA pneumonia.

wholeQuestion.question: Which principle best characterizes clinical and imaging diagnosis?
choices: A new infiltrate plus infectious clinical evidence supports HAP or VAP, but no gold standard exists
A new infiltrate alone proves that the lung abnormality has an infectious cause
Purulent secretions alone provide a definitive diagnosis regardless of imaging or clinical trajectory
Clinical evidence can be ignored once an imaging abnormality is present
wholeQuestion.rationale: Interpret a new lung infiltrate together with clinical evidence of infection, such as new fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis, or declining oxygenation. No gold standard exists for HAP or VAP diagnosis. An infiltrate or secretion change alone does not establish the full diagnosis; reassess discordant findings and alternative explanations.

wholeQuestion.question: Which principle best characterizes HAP MSSA and gram-negative frame?
choices: Empiric HAP therapy covers S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, and other gram-negative bacilli, with MRSA coverage when indicated
Empiric HAP therapy can cover gram-negative bacilli alone and omit all S. aureus coverage
Empiric HAP therapy can cover MSSA alone and omit P. aeruginosa and other gram-negative bacilli
Empiric HAP therapy needs P. aeruginosa coverage only after a positive culture has already identified it
wholeQuestion.rationale: Build empiric HAP therapy to cover S. aureus together with P. aeruginosa and other gram-negative bacilli. Select MSSA or MRSA coverage and the breadth of antipseudomonal therapy using patient risk factors and local susceptibility data. A positive culture is not a prerequisite for empiric P. aeruginosa coverage; narrow treatment when microbiology and clinical response permit.

wholeQuestion.question: Which principle best characterizes definitive MRSA therapy?
choices: Vancomycin or linezolid is recommended for proven MRSA HAP or VAP
Choose daptomycin for MRSA HAP or VAP because its bloodstream activity guarantees lung activity
Treat proven MRSA HAP or VAP with an MSSA-only antibiotic instead of MRSA-active therapy
Use an antipseudomonal agent with no MRSA activity as the sole definitive treatment for proven MRSA HAP or VAP
wholeQuestion.rationale: For MRSA HAP or VAP, ATS/IDSA recommends vancomycin or linezolid. Choose between them using patient-specific factors, including renal function, blood cell counts and interacting medicines. Daptomycin is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant and should not be used to treat pneumonia. MSSA-only or gram-negative-only activity does not replace MRSA-active definitive therapy.
